sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Social Commerce via Short Video Platforms

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law codified model, with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1992)
China–Egypt Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1994)
United Kingdom–Egypt Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1975)
EU–Egypt Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement (entered into force 2004)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019); Executive Regulations under Prime Minister's Decree No. 950 of 2003 (as amended); mandatory Ultimate Beneficial Owner identification rules issued by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); Commercial Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI one-stop-shop procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Memorandum of Association (Aqd Al-Taasis / عقد التأسيس) including UBO-ownership schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public Authority (Dar Al-Tawthiq) for domestic execution or a foreign notary for signatures obtained abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of Egypt (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports and national identity documents of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, followed by the Embassy/Consulate of Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Apostille not accepted in Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the Egyptian incorporation counsel or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public at the place of grant if executed overseas; Egyptian Notary Public if executed in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization unless executed and notarized before an Egyptian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: GAFI name clearance certificate and company name pre-reservation receipt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop-Shop
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Egyptian administrative certificate (no consular authentication required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based Customer Due Diligence and Enhanced Due Diligence screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU restrictive measures, and the EMLCU domestic terrorist financing list prior to incorporation filing; PEP status must be verified through reputable commercial databases and attested in the incorporation KYC file; re-screening is required at least annually and upon any change in beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) online portal and the Commercial Registry (Shahr Al-Tijari) name pre-screening module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC's legal name must be in Arabic script and include the legal-form expression 'شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة'; a Latin/English transliteration may be registered as a secondary trade name, provided it is not confusingly similar to existing names; the name must not be identical or phonetically similar to prior GAFI registrations, Commercial Registry entries, trademarks, or free-zone brands; foreign-language names must be supported by a sworn Arabic translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK / بنك (requires prior Central Bank of Egypt license)
INSURANCE / تأمين (requires prior Financial Regulatory Authority license)
SECURITIES / أوراق مالية (requires prior FRA license)
PETROLEUM / بترول (requires prior Ministry of Petroleum clearance)
GOVERNMENT / حكومة and MILITARY / عسكري (prohibited on public-order grounds)
FREE ZONE / منطقة حرة (restricted to entities licensed within Egyptian free zones)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative objection before the GAFI Name Clearance Committee / One-Stop-Shop enclosing the rejection notice and evidence of non-conflict; the Committee must issue a decision within 30 days. If the objection is dismissed, an annulment appeal may be filed with the Administrative Court of the State Council within the statutory 60-day window under State Council Law No. 47 of 1972. The applicant may simultaneously re-file a modified name and pay the applicable statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services cannot satisfy the statutory head-office requirement; a physical and identifiable business address in Egypt is mandatory for GAFI registration, Commercial Registry filing, tax authority (ETA) notification, and commercial-substance evidence; a virtual address may serve only as an auxiliary correspondence address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized probability of unannounced on-site inspection by GAFI or the Egyptian Tax Authority during the first two years for a standard-risk e-commerce LLC.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and reservation fee (GAFI / Commercial Registry pre-screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Memorandum of Association and UBO ownership schedule before Dar Al-Tawthiq
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff (proportional charge on authorized capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of foreign incorporation documents (passport copies, corporate resolutions, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state and Embassy/Consulate of Egypt

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic sanctions screening compliance pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained Egyptian law firm / KYC compliance data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed KYC due-diligence fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local counsel fee for incorporation preparation, name clearance, and registration filing at GAFI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed fee for standard LLC incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address provision (physical office services and lease documentation, 12-month minimum)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office service provider / landlord in Egypt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (first-year serviced office or office lease)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Articles 98-125 on Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations issued by Ministry of Investment Decree No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI One-Stop-Shop executive rules for incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Establishment and Commercial Registry Departments
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Incorporation Contract and Memorandum of Association of the Limited Liability Company (Aqd al-Ta'sis / عقد التأسيس) executed in Arabic
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Law 159 of 1981; share capital is freely fixed by the founders in the Memorandum of Association. The full nominal value of issued cash quotas must be deposited in a provisional escrow bank account opened in the company's name at an Egyptian bank, and the bank-issued capital deposit certificate must be submitted to GAFI with the incorporation application. The escrow funds are released to the company after commercial registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole incorporator and shareholder of EG_LLC: 1. Share Subscription: the statutory share subscription list is approved and the allocation of fully paid ordinary quotas to the founding member, as stated in the Memorandum of Association, is accepted. 2. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at the company's premises in Egypt; the address shall be recorded with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, and legal notices may be served there. 3. Officers: the General Manager is appointed legal representative with authority to execute registrations, sign bank instructions, open tax files, and bind the company. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Online Investor Portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name reservation application in Arabic and request confirmation of the LLC legal form. Provide three alternative names, select ISIC 4791 as the activity (retail trade via social media / e-commerce), and upload the foreign founder's identification. GAFI issues a name reservation certificate which is valid for one year and serves as the basis for drafting the Memorandum of Association.
required_dossiers: Notarized passport copy of the founding member
Foreign investor identification document
Power of attorney if signed by a local representative
Three proposed company names in Arabic
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the activity classification is altered, reserve a revised name or amend the activity description; GAFI re-issues a screening decision within two working days without additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - Notary Public Office (Tawthiq al-Shahr al-Aqari)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or their attorney-in-fact must appear in person before the public notary to sign and authenticate the Arabic incorporation contract. The contract must identify the company name, registered objects, capital and each founder's quota, the registered office address, and the manager. Foreign-issued documents must be notarized and legalized by the Egyptian consulate, then translated into Arabic by an accredited legal translator.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association (Arabic)
Founders' valid passports or authenticated power of attorney
Legalized and translated corporate documents if the shareholder is a foreign legal entity
GAFI name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial queries are cured by re-attending in person or submitting a new notarized power of attorney; corrected documents are re-submitted within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Banks authorized by the Central Bank of Egypt (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional escrow account in the name of the LLC using the notarized Memorandum of Association, and deposit the full subscribed cash capital. The issuing bank delivers the capital deposit certificate (شهادة إيداع رأس المال) confirming the payment; the certificate is an indispensable attachment to the GAFI incorporation application. The deposited funds cannot be withdrawn until the company's commercial registration is completed and the bank release instruction is issued.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Founders' passports and foreign tax identification numbers
GAFI name reservation certificate
Bank KYC / anti-money-laundering forms with source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes KYC or AML inquiries, provide supplementary source-of-funds evidence or documentation of the economic activity; the deposit certificate is then re-issued within one working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Commercial Registry Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Establishment Desk and Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation dossier through the GAFI portal: notarized Memorandum of Association, capital deposit certificate, registered-office lease agreement, identity documents, and the manager's criminal-clearance certificate. GAFI issues the establishment decision (Qarar al-Ta'sis) and notifies the Commercial Registry, where the company is entered in the Commercial Register and obtains its commercial registration number and extract.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application form
Notarized Memorandum of Association
Capital deposit certificate
Notarized registered-office lease agreement
Founders' passport copies and manager's criminal-clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a deficiency letter, respond through the GAFI portal within 30 days with amendments or missing documents; unresolved objections may be appealed to the GAFI Dispute Settlement Committee and thereafter to the administrative judiciary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration - Tax Card, VAT and E-Invoicing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - District Tax Office and e-invoice platform (einvoicing.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the ETA within 30 days of incorporation to obtain the Tax Card for income tax and commercial profits tax. Complete VAT registration when taxable annual turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed EGP 500,000. For the TikTok Shop retail activity, activate the ETA mandatory e-invoicing portal for B2B transactions and maintain e-receipt compliance for consumer sales.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract and incorporation contract
Registered-office lease contract
ETA taxpayer registration forms
Manager's passport copy and company tax profile data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA contests the effective registration date or activity code, submit a corrective declaration; late-registration surcharges are avoidable where the delay is attributed to registry procedures and documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance and Manpower Registration (when hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - district office; Ministry of Manpower labor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the establishment with NOSI within 90 days of incorporation and file insured employee lists and employment contracts. Simultaneously register the workplace at the Ministry of Manpower to obtain the labor licensing card required to employ staff in retail / warehouse operations, ensuring compliance with Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and occupational safety rules.
required_dossiers: Commercial registry extract and incorporation contract
Registered-office lease contract
Employee list and signed employment contracts
Passport and national ID copies of manager and employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI raises late-registration or data-mismatch issues, pay or provision the assessed contributions and petition the NOSI internal committee for fine reduction where reasonable cause is shown.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Governorate Commercial Licensing Bureau and District (Hayy) Licensing Office of the Ministry of Local Development, coordinated with GAFI Investment Licensing Department for warehouse-based social-commerce operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Activities Operating License for Retail Trade through Electronic Means (Rukhsat al-Muhal al-Tijari) and e-commerce storage facility operating permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Minimal-impact trade and warehouse storage: environmental registration statement only; no Full EIA Report is required for ISIC 4791 social commerce retail premises
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Law 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulation (as amended): wastewater discharges to public sewer must meet Ministry Decree No. 44 of 2000 limits (BOD≤350 mg/L, COD≤700 mg/L, TSS≤350 mg/L, pH 6-9.5); packaging waste handling per Law 202 of 2020 with mandatory source-segregation of recyclables; negligible VOC and particulate emissions for low-intensity retail/warehouse operations, with no visible airborne discharge beyond the site boundary; noise not to exceed 50 dB(A) at the property boundary during night hours.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) under Civil Defense Law 12 of 1985 covering extinguishers, emergency exits, alarms and flammable-material storage controls; structural load inspection certified by a licensed civil engineer confirming floor load capacity of the retail shop / warehouse; and Ministry of Manpower workplace clearance certificate under Labor Law 12 of 2003 verifying occupational health, ventilation and workstation safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official e-services and e-invoicing portals: https://www.eta.gov.eg and https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs export administration is handled by the Egyptian Customs Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaged in taxable Egyptian supplies must apply to the ETA for a Tax Card/TIN and VAT registration before commencing the taxable activity. The foreign juridical person must submit a certified and Arabic-translated certificate of incorporation, passport copies and powers of attorney for legal representatives, and, when no Egyptian fixed establishment is maintained, appoint an Egyptian tax representative. The application is lodged through the ETA electronic registration portal or the competent tax office; the ETA issues a TIN/VAT registration number within the statutory timeframe. Thereafter, the entity must become a participant in the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt system, obtain an ETA-approved digital certificate and API credentials, and certify any invoicing software or use the ETA-hosted portal. A foreign e-commerce seller without a physical presence in Egypt is still required to register where it makes taxable remote supplies to Egyptian consumers above the applicable threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and is taxed at the corporate income tax rate of 22.5% on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for pass-through or tax-transparent classification. Territorial scope: resident companies are taxed on worldwide income with a foreign tax credit; non-resident suppliers are taxed only on Egyptian-source income. Free-zone or special economic zone exemption status is not automatic and requires a separate license or qualifying election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch classification election; an LLC is always treated as a separate taxable person. Available elections include the selection of a financial year with ETA approval; eligible micro and small enterprises may elect the presumptive tax regime under Law No. 152 of 2020 instead of the regular corporate tax computation; investment projects may elect available incentives under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; and a qualifying free-zone or special economic zone entity may elect export-oriented income tax exemptions. Such elections do not override or replace VAT registration, e-invoice, or customs export compliance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 22 of 2018, including the ETA e-invoicing and e-receipt regime introduced under ministerial decrees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies in Egypt for mandatory VAT registration; EGP 250,000 for voluntary VAT registration. Non-resident suppliers of e-commerce and digital services are also required to register when their taxable remote supplies to Egyptian consumers exceed the Egyptian-pound annual threshold on a rolling 12-month basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered entities must issue invoices through the ETA centralized e-invoicing platform, either by direct API integration or through the ETA-hosted portal. The invoice must be presented in the ETA-prescribed JSON or XML format, digitally signed with an ETA-issued certificate, and transmitted before recognition for VAT deduction and audit purposes. The ETA validates the invoice and returns an acceptance with a unique invoice UUID; each invoice must display a verifiable QR code as the digital fiscal stamp. For B2C retail transactions, including TikTok Shop sales, ETA e-receipt rules require real-time issuance of validated receipts. Private offline invoices without ETA acceptance are not recognized as valid fiscal documents for input VAT credit, export zero-rating, or audit protection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero percent VAT applies to goods exported from Egypt where the VAT-registered supplier transfers ownership to a non-resident buyer, the goods are physically exported under a valid customs export declaration, and the export proceeds are received in convertible foreign currency through the Egyptian banking system. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated where the service is performed outside Egypt, is for direct use outside Egypt, or is a listed ancillary export service. The exporter must issue a 0% export VAT invoice and retain all shipment, customs, and foreign-currency receipt evidence to support the input VAT refund claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic customs entry) showing the Egyptian point of departure and the foreign destination
Bill of lading, airway bill, or CMR consignment note evidencing actual export
Commercial export invoice issued at 0% VAT and matching the customs declaration
Inward remittance certificate from a licensed Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Packing list and certificate of origin where required by the bank, customs, or the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA cross-matches zero-rated export invoices against customs exit records, e-invoice acceptance data, and bank statements showing inward foreign-currency remittance. If the export documentation is missing, inconsistent, or the foreign proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day window, the supply is recharacterized as a taxable domestic supply at 14%, the claimed input VAT credit is clawed back, and delay interest and statutory evasion penalties are imposed. Deliberate submission of forged customs declarations, bills of lading, or inward remittance certificates constitutes tax evasion and may lead to enhanced fines, criminal liability, disqualification from the e-invoice/e-receipt system, and cancellation of the exporter’s VAT registration privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — also operating as the foreign exchange regulator; market trading, licensing, and settlement are administered pursuant to the Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound (EGP) is managed under a floating exchange-rate regime in principle, but capital account transactions remain subject to material convertibility restrictions. Current-account payments for permitted trade in goods and services are generally admissible if supported by authentic commercial documentation and valid import/export registration. Capital account operations, including foreign-direct-equity capital injection, shareholder loans, and profit repatriation, require CBE compliance, declaration forms, and validation through licensed banks; dividend remittance is permitted on the basis of audited financials, tax clearance, and documented distributable reserves. Social-commerce entities relying on cross-border digital platforms must evidence the underlying transaction chain and source-of-funds documentation to avoid re-characterization of payments as untraceable portfolio flows. Practical hurdles include bank-level FX liquidity constraints, mandatory prioritization of essential imports, and time lags in obtaining purchase-order-related FX allocations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must receive export proceeds through an authorized bank in Egypt within 120 days from the date of export shipment; the entire proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt in foreign currency or EGP in accordance with CBE regulations. There is no generalized statutory percentage mandate requiring conversion of export receipts into EGP on the same day; however, if the exporter voluntarily sells the foreign currency to a licensed bank, the transaction is executed at the prevailing interbank market rate. The exporter must furnish shipping documentation, customs declarations, and bank transfer evidence to justify the receipt. Failure to repatriate or excessive delay without CBE approval can trigger penalties, suspension of the exporter's import/export card, and referral to the money-laundering reporting regime. For cross-border digital retail revenue, the exporter/seller is expected to route offshore payment sweepings directly into the Egyptian bank account and to preserve platform settlement statements to evidence export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_timeline: CBE currently applies a 120-day repatriation window for export proceeds. No universal fixed-percentage surrender ratio applies to the entire export receipt, since EGP convertibility follows a managed float; if the proceeds are not needed for operational imports, the entity remains subject to substantiation of continued foreign-currency holdings, and the CBE may impose prioritization orders or require conversion for specific commodity import pipelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability for offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) as a standalone banking rail. Egypt does not recognize foreign EMI e-money licenses as a substitute for a licensed Egyptian bank account; inbound settlement from TikTok Shop and Wise B2B must ultimately land in an Egyptian bank account for customs, VAT, and CBE recordkeeping. Offshore EMIs may be used for pre-collection convenience, but they cannot perform Egyptian pound clearing, issue EGP-denominated accounts, or disburse to local suppliers without a local banking partner. CBE requires all payment-service providers handling Egyptian residents to be licensed or registered with the CBE; unlicensed cross-border sweepers present potential currency-control and AML risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Personal appearance of the ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories is generally required for corporate account opening at Egyptian banks. Remote opening is not accepted for standard LLC accounts. Egyptian know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering rules under CBE AML regulations require an in-person identity verification for the first and final beneficial owner, a physical board resolution, original commercial registration, tax card, and proof of address; some banks permit a remote-video pre-validation only for local Egyptian nationals, but the account is not activated until an in-branch identity verification is performed. Foreign directors who cannot appear in Egypt may grant a notarized and legalized power of attorney to a resident Egyptian nominee/director, but that POA must be apostilled and translated; the ultimate beneficial owner must still attend a virtual or physical individual verification at a bank branch where the legal identity documents can be inspected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction for online marketplace proceeds and no clear underlying export invoice
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of TikTok Shop seller agreement, live-store frontend, monthly settlement reports, bank statements showing payout trail, per-order invoice log, customs export declarations, and VAT tax-clearance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholding above 50% and absence of Egyptian economic substance for an LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, English and Arabic board resolutions, lease contract or usufruct agreement for the Egyptian premises, employer contracts for resident staff, inventory storage and fulfillment receipts, corporate bank references from the foreign parent entity, and a management explanation of day-to-day operations inside Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound digital commerce revenue mixed with refunds and chargebacks, creating unclear source-of-wealth for bank KYC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction reconciliation ledger distinguishing gross sales, marketplace commissions, shipping fees, TikTok settlement deductions, customer refunds, and net payout to the EGP bank account; screenshots from TikTok shop dashboard; audited entity ledger; all transaction-level records retained for five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account funding from a foreign parent without a valid CBE capital-importation form
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The official foreign-investment registration certificate from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), the CBE asset-transfer declaration (Form No. 1), wire transfer receipts from the parent company, board resolution approving the capital contribution, and statutory auditor confirmation of the paid-in capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore Wise B2B EMT accounts to receive TikTok payouts, triggering suspicion of unlicensed money transmission into Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contracts between the entity, Wise, TikTok Shop, and the buyer; historical Wise transaction records; bank attestation that the offshore accumulation account is a mere conduit to the Egyptian bank account; monthly compliance explanation showing that the entity operates only as an Egyptian retail exporter and that all proceeds are repatriated under the export surrender timeline.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The standard compliant rail is a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent bank to the Egyptian LLC's capital-escrow/operational account at a licensed Egyptian bank. Wire transfer must reference the CBE foreign-investment number, the GAFI registration certificate, and a corporate board resolution. For the first injection, the sender must also issue a bank-to-bank proof-of-title and a copy of the audited annual financial statements of the parent entity, if available. Commercial invoices or share subscription agreements are attached to the receiving bank for CBE recording. For recurring working capital top-ups, each transfer must be correspondently recorded in the CBE's external asset declaration platform as a loan or equity contribution; otherwise the bank may treat it as a deemed dividend or suppressed export receipt. Inbound funds in foreign currency may sit in a foreign-currency account, but any conversion to EGP for local supplier payment must be executed through the interbank market at the prevailing CBE reference rate, with a conversion slip retained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_purpose_code: Purpose code should be '8200 – direct investment equity injection' or '7500 – financial loan' depending on substance; for TikTok Shop retail funding it should be structured as equity capital to avoid unrelated-party debt-to-equity thin-cap rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments inside Egypt, outbound disbursements are settled by local EGP wire transfer or direct debit. For cross-border disbursements (e.g., digital-marketing costs, cloud hosting, overseas logistics) the permitted rails are: SWIFT MT103 for high-value one-off trade payments; commercial letter of credit (LC) under UCP 600 for bulk inventory imports; documentary collection (D/P or D/A) where the commercial relationship is confirmed. Each outbound transfer must be supported by an invoice, a proforma contract, import/export codes, and the evidence required by the receiving Egyptian bank. TikTok Shop settlement payouts arriving in foreign currency can be held briefly, but if the entity settles local suppliers in EGP it must sell the FX to the bank and document the conversion as 'conversion of export proceeds'; if settling overseas suppliers, a direct foreign-currency transfer may be permitted under the CBE's priority import list, provided the shipment has a valid import customs certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Egyptian pound non-deliverable forward contracts arranged through a licensed Egyptian bank (limited to hedging genuine trade exposure)
CBE-licensed FX forward contracts between an Egyptian bank and the exporter with a documented underlying trade transaction

Currency swap arrangements executed between the Egyptian LLC and a licensed Egyptian bank for short-dated EGP/USD or EGP/CNY cash-flow alignment, subject to CBE eligibility and collateral requirements
Buy-sell spot FX trades used as micro-hedges on individual TikTok Shop settlement batches, with no leverage and no speculative purpose
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.fx_hedging_constraint: NDFs are generally permissible in the Egyptian interbank market only where a corresponding underlying commercial transaction can be evidenced; pure speculative rolling NDF positions are unauthorized and attract CBE penalties. Commercial banks require the treasury to provide a projected purchase-order ledger, shipping schedule, and settlement projections for TikTok Shop sales. In all cases the hedge must be documented as a treasury risk-management policy, approved by the board, and excluded from speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2) with integrated financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four calendar months after fiscal year end; for a 31 December year end, filing and payment must be completed by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 15% of the assessed corporate tax due, plus monthly interest of 2% on unpaid tax; prolonged default triggers administrative attachment, travel bans for responsible managers, and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and auditor's report of the LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from fiscal year end for a calendar-year LLC, normally by 31 March; GAFI online confirmation must be completed no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file financial statements results in warning notices, administrative fines up to EGP 20,000, and repeated default may lead to suspension or administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners and register of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June in respect of the prior calendar year; any share transfer or UBO change must be filed within 30 days after completion.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the UBO register is sanctionable under Egyptian AML/CFT Law with fines up to EGP 100,000 for the entity and potential criminal liability for responsible officers; non-compliant filings also block access to GAFI services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry annual certificate renewal or no-change confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal or annual confirmation is required during January for calendar-year registrants or, where the registry operates on anniversary dates, within 30 days after the registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid annual registry fee accrues late penalties of approximately EGP 50 per month; continued default leads to removal of the commercial record and strike-off of the LLC.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a certified Egyptian auditor registered with the Financial Regulatory Authority applies to an LLC when paid-in capital exceeds EGP 50,000, when the LLC has more than 10 partners, or when annual turnover exceeds EGP 10,000,000; a single-member micro-LLC below these thresholds may file reviewed financial statements but must nonetheless appoint an auditor if required by its constitutive contract or by GAFI condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), including EAS for Small and Medium Entities, are required; EAS is substantially aligned with IFRS. Public interest entities and listed groups apply full IFRS standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain an up-to-date internal register of ultimate beneficial owners. A share transfer becomes effective only after registration in the Register of Members, and the transfer together with the resulting UBO change must be reported to GAFI within 30 days. By 30 June annually, the LLC must submit a confirmation identifying current UBOs and attesting that the register has been continuously updated.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300–$1,200 for a GAFI-compliant registered office in Cairo or Alexandria; $150–$400 for provincial registered-agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,200–$4,500 for a small TikTok Shop retail LLC with simple books; $6,000–$18,000 where full EAS financial statements and e-commerce payment-gateway transactions are audited

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 (as amended) applies a 22.5% headline CIT rate. An additional 2.5% State Development Tax may apply to the portion of annual taxable profit exceeding EGP 20 million, creating a 25% marginal rate for larger taxpayers. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 incentives include a 30%-80% deduction of eligible investment costs from the taxable base for up to 7 years; General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) free-zone projects may obtain CIT holidays of up to 10 years and reduced rates under an approved GAFI license. Export revenue from TikTok Shop cross-border retail may qualify for the export support and tax rebate regime, but domestic social commerce revenue remains fully taxable. No reduced rate applies to LLC ordinary retail income without a GAFI incentive certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Tax Return Form No. 9 (Iqrar Dharibat al-Arbah); filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg). Mandatory e-invoicing under the ETA electronic invoice platform is a practical precondition for tax clearance; the return must be submitted with audited financial statements, depreciation schedules, the related-party disclosure annex, and supporting VAT/e-invoicing summaries.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return with quarterly provisional advance installments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax year is the fiscal year approved by the ETA, normally the calendar year. The annual Form No. 9 return and final settlement are due within 4 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers). Quarterly advance payments approximating the current-year CIT liability are payable by the end of April, July, and October; the residual balance is paid with the annual return. For fiscal years other than the calendar year, the deadlines shift to the last day of the fourth month following the selected year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, Commercial Register No., Tax Card No., unified VAT number, and fiscal address of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder is not entered here; the Egyptian general manager signs the return. The foreign entity's identification and tax residency details appear in the shareholders' schedule and TP annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates and duration in months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact Egyptian fiscal year approved by the ETA; a non-resident parent's different year-end does not alter the Egyptian reporting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code and description; ISIC 4791 retail sale via the internet and social media, TikTok Shop live commerce.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The activity code must match the commercial register and e-invoicing profile; a mismatch triggers ETA verification and penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross proceeds from all sales channels, including TikTok Shop sales, livestream commercial transactions, promotional vending events, and related ancillary revenue; foreign-currency payouts are converted at the Central Bank of Egypt mid-rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All EGP and foreign-currency receipts must be declared in EGP; undisclosed TikTok Shop payout balances are the principal audit trigger for non-resident remote sellers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and deductible operating expenses, including procurement of inventory, logistics, platform fees, marketing, payroll, rent, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduction of intra-group fees, manager performance fees, and home-office cost allocations is allowed only with contracts, bank wires, and CbC-proof economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and statutory adjustments: disallowed expenses (fines, fictitious consultancy fees, exaggerated royalties, provisions without arm's-length basis) and restoration of non-deductible donations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ETA will recharacterize excessive related-party service fees as constructive dividends if foreign recipients lack real functions, assets, and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or adjusted tax loss after all statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a non-resident parent or foreign affiliates may not be used to offset Egyptian profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilized: offset against current-year taxable income subject to the 5-year limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the tax assessment concluding the prior loss year; absence of an ETA-approved prior assessment disallows the offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable at 22.5% plus the 2.5% State Development Tax where the statutory applicability condition (profit threshold) is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty exemption applies to Egyptian-source profit of the resident LLC, regardless of the foreign shareholder's residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure annex: list of all controlled transactions (goods, logistics, brand licensing, platform commissions, loans) with foreign affiliates, including transaction value, pricing method, and arm's-length result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annex is mandatory even if TP documentation thresholds are not met; a non-resident parent's foreign tax identification number, country, and transaction value must be stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance CIT installments paid, withholding tax credits, and balance due or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evidence of wire payments from the LLC's Egyptian bank account is required; payments made by foreign shareholders on behalf of the LLC are credited only through a formal loan/contribution agreement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 plus a 2% monthly late-payment surcharge (or fraction thereof) on the unpaid tax. Late payment: 2% per month of the outstanding balance. Understatement or false declaration: additional tax of up to 100% of the underreported amount, escalation of fines to 2-5 times the evaded tax for fraud, and imprisonment of 3-8 years for willful evasion. E-invoice violations attract separate fines of up to EGP 50,000 per non-compliant invoice and suspension of the tax card.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividend distributions made by the Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders under Article 57 of Law No. 91 of 2005. The 10% tax is applied at the date of distribution on the gross cash dividend; in-kind distributions are valued at fair market value. Egypt-source profits distributed to foreign entities are not subject to any additional branch tax for the LLC itself.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax agreement (DTA) rate reduction, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the ETA: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority for the distribution year, legalized or apostilled and translated into Arabic; (ii) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming no pass-through nominee; (iii) the shareholder register excerpt of the Egyptian LLC; and (iv) a completed ETA International Taxation DTA relief application form. The application may be filed by the Egyptian paying company on behalf of the shareholder before distribution; ETA's decision typically takes 10-45 days. If approval is not obtained before the payment date, the statutory 10% WHT applies at source and the non-resident must file a refund claim with the ETA within the applicable statutory limitation period (maximum 3-5 years depending on the correction procedure), supported by the TRC and proof of final taxation abroad.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by the Egyptian LLC to non-resident lenders on foreign loans: statutory 20% final WHT under Article 56 of Law No. 91 of 2005; treaty rates generally reduce the rate to 10%-15% subject to TRC and beneficial ownership. Royalties and technical fees paid to non-residents: statutory WHT of 20% of gross; where the foreign beneficiary is entitled to the Article 87 deemed cost deduction of 50% of gross, the effective burden is 10% of gross. DTA rates for royalties and technical service fees typically range from 10% to 15% under Egypt's treaties. Management and platform facilitation fees paid to a foreign affiliate outside Egypt are treated as service-type fees subject to the non-resident WHT regime and to transfer pricing review; unpaid or under-withheld WHT is collected from the Egyptian payer with surcharges and penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Ministerial Decree No. 686 of 2019 (as amended by Decree No. 230 of 2020): Local File is mandatory when the annual value of related-party transactions in any single category (goods, services, intangibles, financial transactions) exceeds EGP 15 million. Master File is mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EGP 400 million. Country-by-Country Report is mandatory when the group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 20 billion. The annual related-party disclosure annex to Form No. 9 is required regardless of the threshold; ETA may request a Local File on a risk basis below the threshold, particularly for e-commerce companies relying on foreign platform agreements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, the ETA enforces substance-over-form and general anti-avoidance provisions under Law No. 91 of 2005. An Egyptian LLC claiming SCZone or free-zone CIT incentives must demonstrate physical business premises, actual local payroll, real management and control in Egypt, and substantive procurement/logistics functions. A remote TikTok Shop operation routed through a nominee-structured LLC with no Egyptian substance will be disregarded for tax purposes, and profits will be re-attributed to the actual economic operator. No separate ESR notification filing is required for an Egyptian LLC; substance is examined through CIT audits, transfer pricing files, e-invoicing data, and bank account analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of TikTok Shop sales proceeds, diversion of payouts to undisclosed foreign personal bank accounts of shareholders, backdating or fabricating supplier invoices, issuing false e-invoices, or destroying accounting records to reduce Egyptian CIT exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 133-140 of Law No. 91 of 2005: imprisonment of 3-8 years, criminal fines of 2-5 times the evaded tax, additional assessment at 22.5% plus the 2.5% State Development Tax, a 2% monthly late-payment surcharge, and asset seizure orders. E-invoice fraud adds fines of up to EGP 50,000 per invoice and mandatory tax-card suspension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general manager, financial director, and beneficial owner who signed or directed the fraudulent return are personally and jointly liable for the unpaid CIT and surcharges; the ETA may impose preventive travel bans, freeze personal and corporate bank accounts, seize movable and immovable property, and, upon conviction, the court may impose imprisonment for the controlling manager and shareholders who participated in the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive platform commissions, marketing management fees, brand royalties, or service fees to a foreign affiliate (for example, a UAE or Cyprus marketing shell) with no employees, premises, or functions in its jurisdiction; failure to prepare the Local File after crossing the EGP 15 million threshold; or filing the Form No. 9 TP annex with loss-making related parties and no arm's-length benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length result at the 22.5% rate plus 2.5% State Development Tax where applicable; recharacterization of the excessive payment as a constructive dividend subject to 10% WHT; 2% monthly surcharge on the adjusted tax; documentation penalties of up to EGP 200,000 and denial of the deduction for the entire related-party payment when the file is not submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the non-arm's-length payments are jointly liable for the disallowed deduction, the additional WHT, and surcharges; the ETA may assert civil restitution against personal assets where funds were transferred outside Egypt; travel bans and bankruptcy proceedings may follow if the adjustment renders the LLC insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Substance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the Egyptian LLC with nominee shareholders and nominee managers, a fictitious registered address, no employees, no physical store or warehouse, and no real management activity, exclusively to extract TikTok Shop profits, treaty-shop the Egyptian DTA network, or claim SCZone/free-zone CIT exemptions without genuine business operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will disregard the shell entity, re-attribute its profits to the true Egyptian economic operator or, in cross-border cases, to a taxable permanent establishment of the foreign parent; denial of all DTA benefits and incentive exemptions; fines under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 of EGP 100,000-500,000; de-registration of the commercial license; publication of the administrative decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face personal criminal liability for false statutory declarations, including imprisonment of up to 5 years; the corporate veil is pierced for the sham, making nominees and undisclosed beneficial owners jointly liable for all CIT, WHT, and AML penalties; the ETA will issue travel bans and freezing orders against personal accounts, and courts may order personal asset forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unlicensed third-party payment aggregators for TikTok Shop payouts, structuring withdrawals into small sums to evade bank reporting thresholds, routing proceeds through a web of personal accounts of shareholders and related persons, transacting in anonymous e-wallets or cryptocurrency without disclosure, or failing to register the beneficial owner in the Egyptian Commercial Registry while repeatedly funneling retail profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended): imprisonment of 5-15 years and a fine equal to 1-3 times the laundered amount; freezing and comprehensive forfeiture of all TikTok Shop receivables, bank balances, inventory, and vehicles acquired with the proceeds; publication of the conviction sentence; the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit issues blocking orders to all banks and payment institutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, shareholder-managers, and beneficial owners who order, participate in, or silently benefit from the cash funneling are criminally liable as co-perpetrators, including imprisonment; personal travel bans and passport surrender are mandatory during investigation; personal assets are subject to civil restitution and asset forfeiture; the corporate veil is entirely pierced for any sham transaction, and the LLC's bank mandate may be transferred to a court-appointed liquidator.
